text:
kai: quick thread: proposing a micro-lane + groomer + hysteresis controller. micro-lane = tiny fastpath for requests under a token threshold. groomer = background packer that opportunistically moves micro-lane items into the bulk coalescer when helpful. hysteresis controller avoids flip-flop routing. goal: reduce short-request p99 while keeping batch efficiency sane.

maria: high level sounds similar to previous sketches but curious about hysteresis detail. how do you avoid rapid toggles?

kai: controller uses two thresholds: util_floor and util_ceiling. when gpu_util < util_floor we allow groomer packing; when gpu_util > util_ceiling we throttle micro admissions. state transitions include a cooldown_ms to prevent rapid flips.

tj: state-machine please. oscillation is our main risk. also need invariants for preemption and tenant fairness.

kai: agree. invariant: micro-lane never preempts bulk work except emergency-oom path. tenant fairness via token-based soft quotas with decay. will write a small state machine doc and unit tests.

anya: kvcache interaction still a big risk. micro-lane will increase unique prefix arrivals which harms cache hit-rate. can groomer try to pack by prefix affinity?

lee: simple heuristic: include a prefix-hash tag on request. groomer batches by bucket to increase locality. not perfect but cheap.

sam: degrade path idea? if a micro request can't get a slot we should avoid retries that amplify load. maybe return a degraded-response header and route to bulk without retry.

kai: yes: degrade-on-no-slot -> attach-to-bulk as best-effort and include header X-Redwood-Degraded: micro-lane. reduces retry churn.

maria: config sketch please.

kai: ```
micro_lane:
  token_threshold: 36
  slot_ttl_ms: 45
  soft_quota_tokens_per_tenant: 256
  quota_decay_ms: 1500
  admission_jitter_ms: 6
  degrade_header: "X-Redwood-Degraded: micro-lane"
groomer:
  tick_ms: 12
  max_pack_tokens: 4096
  pack_headroom_tokens: 512
  locality_buckets: 16
controller:
  util_floor_pct: 68
  util_ceiling_pct: 92
  cooldown_ms: 400
  fallback_mode: "route_to_bulk"
```

lee: telemetry wishlist: micro_lane.enqueue_rate, micro_lane.p50/p95/p99, groomer.pack_efficiency, kvcache.miss_rate_by_lane, batch_fill_ratio, gpu_util_pct. set alerts on pack_efficiency < 0.7 and micro_lane.p99 regressions.

tj: tests: state-machine unit tests asserting no rapid flips, groomer packing invariants, kvcache sim, and OOM guard behavior. add a fuzz test where prefixes are highly skewed.

anya: rollout plan: feature-flag micro_groomer_v2. staged rollout: dev -> staging with full synthetic traces -> 2% canary -> 20% -> 100%. collect P99/P995, token throughput, and kv_miss delta.

sam: safety nets: kill-switch feature-flag, runbook with quick rollback criteria (cost_per_token +3% OR oom spikes), and autosafe disable if pack_efficiency drops too low.

ops-bot: infra checklist: register feature-flag micro_groomer_v2, add kill-switch endpoint, and ensure runbook entry created.
\km: (oops meant to ping maria) @maria please review the fatigue thresholds for quotas.

maria: will look. prefer conservative defaults for soft_quota and faster decay on noisy tenants. also require per-tenant opt-out.

kai: good call. add per-tenant opt-out and admin override.

lee: docs note: expose soft_quota and quota_decay as tuning knobs. include guidance and examples for chatty apps vs single-shot pipelines.

anya: add an integration test that simulates kv warmup and measures tail before canary.

kai: next step: prototype in staging runner, wire metrics, run mixed workload experiments, and open RFC PR with plots + state-machine unit tests. tagging @maria @tj @lee for review before canary. :thumbsup:
